record.original_question: Under what circumstances can there exist saddle points p and q, together with relatively open sets U⊂W^u(p) and V⊂W^u(q), such that U∩K^+ and V∩K^+ are biholomorphic?

evidence.quote: Question 32. — Under which circumstances is it possible that there exist saddle points p and q, and relative open subsets U ⊂ Wu(p) and V ⊂ Wu(q) such that U ∩ K+ is biholomorphic to V ∩ K+?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f:\mathbb{C}^2 \to \mathbb{C}^2$ be a complex Hénon map, that is, a finite composition of generalized Hénon maps of the form $(x,y)\mapsto (y, p(y)-ax)$ with $a\in\mathbb{C}^*$ and $p$ a polynomial of degree at least $2$. Let $K^+ = \{z\in\mathbb{C}^2 : \{f^n(z)\}_{n\ge 0}\text{ is bounded}\}$ denote the forward filled Julia set. For a saddle periodic point $p$ of $f$, let $W^u(p)$ denote the unstable manifold of $p$, which is biholomorphic to $\mathbb{C}$.

Characterize the circumstances under which there can exist two saddle periodic points $p$ and $q$ of $f$, together with relatively open subsets $U \subset W^u(p)$ and $V \subset W^u(q)$, such that the intersections $U \cap K^+$ and $V \cap K^+$ are biholomorphic (as subsets of the respective Riemann surfaces $W^u(p)$ and $W^u(q)$).
